content:
If you're like me, you've probably spent a few hours on Wikipedia, clicking around and browsing random articles. Now there's finally an official app for it—though honestly, it's more like a small tool for doing just that.

Now there's finally a button that can take you directly to a random Wikipedia article.

An update to the Wikipedia iOS app today added an interesting and practical new feature: a 'Random Article' widget that you can place on your iPhone or iPad home screen.

The widget comes in both large and medium sizes, and even features a cute mascot.

Tap the widget and it will take you to a completely random Wikipedia article, opened in random mode.

You don't need to leave the app and tap the widget again—just hit the random button to keep rolling the dice and delve deeper and deeper into this random maze.

Have fun, but be careful not to lose track of time. Earlier this summer, the Wikipedia app also added a historical trivia mini-game.

After you update the Wikipedia app on your iPhone and iPad today, you'll be able to find this brand-new widget.

Enjoy your Apple devices to the fullest!
